lessons.title: Order Matching Engine
lessons.subtitle: How NASDAQ Processes 1M+ Orders Per Second
lessons.real_obstacle: Knight Capital lost $440M in 45 minutes (Aug 1, 2012) due to a deployment bug that activated old test code in their matching engine

papers.title: The Design of a Financial Exchange

lessons.napkin_math: 1M orders/sec × 100 bytes/order = 100MB/sec throughput. At 50μs latency, need single-threaded hot path (no locks). LMAX Disruptor achieves this with ring buffer.
lessons.ai_smb_angle: Build AI-powered order matching for SMB crypto/stock brokerages using event-driven architecture + ML-based anomaly detection for flash crash prevention. Claude API predicts unusual volume spikes 30sec ahead.
interview_questions: Design an order matching engine that handles 100K orders/sec with <1ms latency
How would you handle partial fills in a limit order book?
What happens when the matching engine crashes mid-trade?

lessons.title: Order Book Data Structure
lessons.subtitle: The Heart of Every Exchange - Price-Time Priority at Nanosecond Speed
lessons.real_obstacle: The 2010 Flash Crash: Dow dropped 1,000 points in 5 minutes. A $4.1B sell order caused cascading order book imbalance. SEC introduced circuit breakers afterward.

papers.title: Limit Order Book Dynamics and Asset Pricing
Price Dynamics in a Markovian Limit Order Market

lessons.napkin_math: 100K updates/sec × 8 bytes per price level × 1000 stocks = 800MB/sec of order book data. Need in-memory sorted structure. Red-black tree: O(log n) insert/delete.
lessons.ai_smb_angle: AI order book analyzer for SMB trading platforms: predict short-term price movements from order book imbalance using transformer models. Real-time anomaly detection flags manipulation.
interview_questions: What data structure would you use for a limit order book and why?
How do you handle the thundering herd problem when a large order hits?
Design a system to detect spoofing in the order book

lessons.title: Market Data Feed Architecture
lessons.subtitle: Distributing Real-Time Prices to Millions of Traders Worldwide
lessons.real_obstacle: Aug 22, 2013: NASDAQ halted trading for 3 hours due to SIP (Securities Information Processor) overload. The consolidated feed couldn't keep up with quote traffic, causing stale prices.
lessons.napkin_math: 10M messages/sec × 200 bytes avg = 2GB/sec. With 1000 subscribers each needing their own copy = 2TB/sec if unicast. Multicast: same 2GB/sec serves all. 1000x bandwidth savings.
lessons.ai_smb_angle: Build AI-filtered market data feeds for SMB brokers: instead of raw firehose, ML models pre-filter relevant signals per user's portfolio. Reduce bandwidth 95% while surfacing only actionable data.
interview_questions: Why does market data use UDP multicast instead of TCP?
How would you handle message gaps in a market data feed?
Design a system to normalize data from 13 different exchanges into one unified feed

lessons.title: Risk Management & Circuit Breakers
lessons.subtitle: How Exchanges Prevent Market Meltdowns
lessons.real_obstacle: March 9, 2020: Circuit breakers triggered 4 times in one week during COVID crash. S&P 500 dropped 7% within minutes of opening bell. System worked as designed but exposed latency in halt propagation across venues.

papers.title: The Role of Circuit Breakers in Market Stability

lessons.napkin_math: Risk check must complete in <5μs to not slow matching engine. At 1M orders/sec, that's 1μs per order budget. Pre-computed risk limits in L1 cache (64 bytes per instrument) = ~64KB for 1000 instruments. Fits in CPU cache.
lessons.ai_smb_angle: AI risk engine for SMB brokerages: real-time position monitoring with ML-based stress testing. Predict portfolio VaR (Value at Risk) using Monte Carlo + neural nets. Auto-hedge suggestions via Claude API.
interview_questions: Design a pre-trade risk check system that adds <10μs latency
How would you implement circuit breakers for a crypto exchange?
What's the tradeoff between risk check thoroughness and latency?

lessons.title: Settlement & Clearing Architecture
lessons.subtitle: T+1: How $1 Trillion Changes Hands Daily Without Losing a Penny
lessons.real_obstacle: GameStop (Jan 2021): DTCC raised collateral requirements 10x overnight. Robinhood needed $3.4B in 24 hours. They restricted buying, causing congressional hearings. Root cause: T+2 settlement meant 2 days of counterparty risk.

papers.title: The Economics of Clearing and Settlement
Blockchain and the Future of Settlement

lessons.napkin_math: Without netting: 10M trades/day × $10K avg = $100T in transfers needed. With netting: 98% cancelled out = $2T actual transfers. Netting saves $98T in daily capital movement.
lessons.ai_smb_angle: AI-powered settlement prediction for SMB brokers: ML predicts settlement fails 24hrs ahead based on counterparty patterns. Smart netting algorithms reduce capital requirements 40%. Blockchain-based instant settlement for SMB trading platforms.
interview_questions: Why can't stock trades settle instantly? What are the technical barriers?
Design a netting system that handles 10M trades per day
How would blockchain change the clearing and settlement process?

lessons.title: Co-location & Latency Arbitrage
lessons.subtitle: Paying $14K/Month for 1 Microsecond Advantage
lessons.real_obstacle: Spread Networks spent $300M to build a fiber optic cable from Chicago to NYC that was 100 miles shorter than existing routes, saving 3ms. Then microwave towers made it obsolete in 2 years. McKay Brothers now does Chicago-NYC in 4.25ms via microwave.
lessons.napkin_math: Light travels 300km/ms in vacuum, ~200km/ms in fiber. NYC-Chicago = 1,200km fiber = 6ms. Microwave through air at ~280km/ms = 4.3ms. 1.7ms advantage × 1000 trades/sec = 1.7 seconds of information advantage per second.
lessons.ai_smb_angle: SMBs can't compete on latency. Instead: AI-powered smart order routing that finds best execution across venues. ML models predict short-term price impact to minimize slippage. Claude API analyzes order flow patterns.
interview_questions: How would you design a system to measure end-to-end latency in microseconds?
What's kernel bypass and why do HFT firms use it?
Design a smart order router that minimizes execution cost

lessons.title: Exchange Fault Tolerance
lessons.subtitle: When Wall Street Goes Dark: Real Outages and How They Were Fixed
lessons.real_obstacle: NYSE July 8, 2015: A software update the night before introduced a configuration issue. Gateway servers rejected connections. Manual failover took 3hrs 38min because the backup systems had a different software version. Cost: estimated $2.4B in trading opportunity.

papers.title: In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm

lessons.napkin_math: 3hr 38min outage × $25B daily volume / 6.5hr trading day = ~$14B in trades that couldn't execute. Even at 0.01% commission = $1.4M in direct revenue loss. Indirect losses: trust, regulatory fines.
lessons.ai_smb_angle: AI-powered chaos engineering for SMB exchanges: automated fault injection testing, ML-predicted failure modes, self-healing infrastructure. Claude API monitors system health and auto-escalates before humans notice.
interview_questions: Design a hot-hot failover system for a matching engine
How do you ensure both replicas process orders in the same sequence?
What's the tradeoff between consistency and availability for a stock exchange?
